entry.title: The Fraud That Was Two Hops Away
entry.summary: At 2:17 AM, a payment request hit our system. Everything looked clean. New phone number. Any normal fraud system would approve it instantly. Ours almost did too. But before the transaction completed, our graph engine performed a relationship traversal — and within 50 milliseconds, it uncovered something surprising. This “clean” transaction was secretly connected to a known fraud case through two hops. And that’s when the transaction was blocked. Most fraud systems treat transactions like isolated events. A payment comes in and we ask questions like: Has this card been reported before? Has this email been used in fraud? Is this phone number suspicious? If everything looks new, the transaction usually passes. And fraudsters know this. So they don't reuse the exact same details. Instead, they…
